outgoing.explanation: The Suffolk Deeds Quinapaug conveyances locate the tract in the Providence jurisdiction and show no recorded Gurney parcel, grounding the unrecorded-share reading of the estate line.

shortLabel: Suffolk Deeds IV - Quinapaug (Providence-jurisdiction) tract, no Gurney in the recorded deeds

sources.alignmentNote: No Gurney among the recorded Quinapaug deeds (pp. 268, 270-271 per the volume index).
sources.locator: Suffolk Deeds Lib. IV pp. 270-271 read via FamilySearch full-text images, film 007442495, image 191 (Hudson to Button; recites Foote's 18 June 1655 Indian purchase and the 1660 conveyance to Hudson)

statement: Suffolk Deeds Liber IV records the Quinapaug tract: Joshua Foote bought 4,000 acres 'att Quinapaug within ye Jurisdiction of Providence' from the Indians Sacont and George Sacount by deed of 18 June 1655; by 1660 it passed to William Hudson, who sold it in 500-acre parcels to Boston men. No Gurney appears among the recorded Quinapaug parcels.
